lead: you have started more lives than you could name and kept no account of any, and the only piece of it with a date on it and witnesses in the room is a promise you said out loud.
sun: inside a marriage the hands go on doing what they do: the second career was got standing at your kitchen table, the move happened because you found the house, the courage arrived as a set of arrangements small enough to say yes to. all of it left your hands the week it worked, and it belongs to them now, honestly theirs, told as their own doing across thirty years of dinners.
moon: the promise was never a feeling. it was entered on purpose, at a fixed hour, with terms said aloud, and it holds through years when nothing else in the house is holding. what it will not do is release. nothing in you carries an instruction for ending a bond, so whether to stay has come up twice in three decades and neither time got as far as a decision.
pull: everything you ever made left without your name on it. the one document your life produced says nothing about what you can do and only what you will not stop doing.
tension: everything else you built was built to run without you, which is why none of it is yours. this one names you personally and cannot be handed on. the year it went bad you had no move — the usual one, put it in somebody else's hands and go, is not performable on a promise — and you sat it out for a winter, doing the one thing nothing in your life had trained you for.
cost: the bad stretch ran three years and neither of you went anywhere, because the thing holding it had never been the state of the feeling. what you put in cannot be totalled by anyone. the promise made it improper to count and your hands were not going to count anyway, so the marriage rests on a figure that has never existed and does not need to.

lead: the list is kept in order of when people joined, and everyone above your line has died or stopped, so when a question comes up now it arrives at you and does not go anywhere afterwards.
sun: for thirty years a thing you said in a corridor became somebody's project and then nobody's in particular, which is how you like it and how any of it survived. that has stopped working. the same sentence now leaves your hands with your standing fastened to it, and nothing shakes that off, and whoever carries it away carries an instruction from somebody nobody outranks.
moon: seniority here came by date and attaches to no post — nobody appointed you, you simply outlasted the line above yours. what it removes is the layer that used to sit over your work, the person who could say leave it. every start goes out unchecked now, and the weight travels one direction, down onto people who joined later and take your recollection as the record.
pull: the push was only ever any good while it was anonymous. now it goes out with a rank on it, and the things you start stand up straight and stop the day you stop.
tension: the handoff has stopped taking. a thing used to leave your hands because somebody wanted it and could carry it as their own. now it is received, brought back for approval at the second obstacle. the people who would once have run with it are junior by decades and treat a start of yours as a standing order. the one motion your life is built on needs somebody willing to take a thing off you as an equal.
cost: nothing in that field takes a season to get standing. you back a thing on a wednesday and by the following week it has rooms, money and people, at a speed only rank buys. everything begun that way is on loan from your position. the ones still running unaided are all from before anybody knew who you were, and the newer ones will finish a year after you do.

lead: at twenty-two you took the whole of where you came from apart to find the actual reason it worked the way it did, and every start your hands have made since came out of that hole.
sun: what leaves your hands begins as a demolition. somebody brings the argument they keep having and you go under it, and by the end of the evening the floor they were standing on is in pieces. then the hands do the other half: something workable, built on the actual cause, in their possession by the weekend. they rebuild on it for years and remember that evening as the night they saw it themselves.
moon: the digging does not have a stopping point in it. what you took apart in yourself at twenty-two, you went on taking apart in the places you have lived since, and about a third of what came down did not want to come down. none of that is traceable either. a collapse arriving through a conversation looks, to the person in it, like a conclusion they reached alone.
pull: wreckage and repair are filed under one name and it is not yours. people leave your table with their floor gone and rebuild on what you handed them and call it theirs.
tension: somebody says that is far enough, and you hear a preference rather than a limit, and the next question is out of your mouth: the request to stop is the one instruction that does not land. it has cost two people who were not in difficulty until you found what their difficulty was. the work you did at the bottom was correct in every particular. correct and survivable are different measures and you carry a gauge for only one.
cost: three plausible causes get eliminated in an afternoon by somebody with no stake in which one survives, and what is left standing afterwards holds weight for years. the hour has no shallow setting. people who wanted a hand with one specific thing get the whole excavation, delivered at the depth it happens to go to, and a proportion of them do not come back at all.

lead: two hundred people stand at the same moment on a cue you made up on a wet tuesday nine years ago, and not a person in the building could say where it came from.
sun: a crowd is the one material that absorbs a start completely: nothing a group does together has an author by the third year. half of what this one does together came off your table — the order of the evening, the thing said at the door, the way a newcomer gets put next to somebody. each went in as a suggestion at a small meeting and is now simply what is done here.
moon: you are in the body of it every week and never quite dissolved into it. the sorting runs the whole time you are standing there: which of these habits carries weight, which is decoration somebody is fond of. and the ones you let lapse take two or three people with them, because a decoration was the whole of somebody's place here.
pull: the room does the thing in unison and you are the one person who remembers it being decided. everyone else received it. you are inside the body and it has yet to lift you.
tension: the hour people come for is the one where nobody decides anything: the room stands, you stand, something carries you. that hour is not available. you can see the joins, having cut most of them, and knowing how a thing was made is a permanent bar to being carried by it. everyone else leaves that building refilled, week after week. you leave it at the weight you came in with, and you have gone back for nine years.
cost: a room that size changes how it does a thing inside a season, without a vote and with nobody at the front arguing for it, which is close to impossible to do to a crowd deliberately. the sorting takes people as well as customs. by now the group is leaner, and five or six names have stopped being said, and nothing connects their leaving to anything that happened.
